frozen_contract.acceptance_gate_interpretation: The frozen text's only explicit, testable acceptance criterion is the shadow-mode comparison (router beats naive natural-baseline on trigger noise/f1 with no success regression). It does not itself specify a promotion mechanism from shadow report-only to an enforcing visibility gate; 'Do not load all skills' is stated as the intended end-state behavior of Modular Skill Visibility, not merely of the shadow comparison step.

current_implementation_state.router_py: src/second_brain/router.py implements route() as a deterministic sparse top-K scorer (+1 positive trigger, -2 negative trigger, +1.5 name-bigram, +0.25 capped-0.5 procedure overlap over active+candidate+shadow pools), selecting only skills scoring >=1.0 up to `max_active` (config/skills.toml [router].max_active, ENFORCED, default 3). Every return path hardcodes `"shadow": True`; there is no branch, flag, or config key that ever produces a non-shadow/enforcing result. The module docstring itself states 'sparse top-K, report-only route'.
current_implementation_state.natural_baseline_and_acceptance: natural_baseline() (naive name-token match) and eval_router() (precision/recall/f1 comparison over a labeled task fixture) implement §113's required shadow-vs-natural comparison. tests/test_router.py::test_eval_router_acceptance asserts router f1 >= natural f1 and passes, proving the §113 acceptance gate for the algorithm itself.
current_implementation_state.consumers: router.route() is called from: cli.py (human `route`/`eval` CLI commands, diagnostic only), credit.py (P3.13 counterfactual with/without-skill attribution -- uses routing as an input to measure a skill's effect, not to gate visibility), hermes_adapter.py:_route_task (result folded only into `selected_routes` telemetry/event-payload fields; explicitly documented as 'advisory... must not suppress the existing bounded AutoInject path'), and model_routing.py:_route_skills (feeds `selected_routes` into `_quality_score()`, a P2.6 per-model skill-performance signal for model selection -- an entirely different concern from skill content visibility).
current_implementation_state.visibility_gate_absence: In hermes_adapter.py:_handle_pre_llm, `selected_routes` (from router.route) and `vmem_context`/`packet` (from autoinject, the actual thing injected into the model's context) are computed independently; `selected_routes` is written only into the telemetry `event_payload` and the response's `selected_routes` field. Nothing reads `selected_routes` to decide which skills' full SKILL.md content is exposed, hidden, or lazily hydrated. grep across brainstem/prime-extension/src for router/skill-visibility/selected_routes/max_active returned zero matches: the Prime extension (this session's own harness integration) has no Brain-owned skill-visibility gate at all.
current_implementation_state.descriptor_catalog_absence: No descriptor-only catalog primitive exists anywhere in src/second_brain (grep for descriptor/catalog/manifest/skill_summary/list_skills in router.py, skillforge.py, cli.py: zero matches). There is no function that exposes a skill's name+description separately from its full instruction body for a host to show cheaply before JIT-loading the selected few.
current_implementation_state.named_module_skills_py: `src/second_brain/skills.py` and `tests/test_skills.py`, named in the frozen roadmap matrix's Implementation Module / Automated Evidence columns, do not exist. `tests/test_skill_lifecycle.py` (2 tests) exists but tests `skillforge.audit_lifecycle()` frontmatter/promotion-readiness auditing (P3.11/P3.14/P3.15 territory) -- it is unrelated to routing or visibility and was miscited as P3.16 evidence in outputs/reports/v1-roadmap-baseline-reaudit.md.
current_implementation_state.historical_live_evidence: telemetry/agent-performance/hermes-Brain-Dev-*.jsonl (2026-08-21/22) contains real `hermes_pre_llm_call` events with a populated `selected_routes` field (e.g. ["lean-code"]) alongside unrelated `mem-*` memory-packet selections -- proving the routing algorithm has executed in real historical Hermes sessions. No event in this telemetry, nor any current-session evidence, shows a skill being withheld or lazily hydrated based on that selection.

reuse_decision: Any future P3.16 implementation must extend the existing router.py sparse top-K algorithm and its natural-baseline/eval_router acceptance harness -- both already proven and must not be redesigned or duplicated. It must NOT create a new `skills.py` module merely to satisfy the frozen matrix's stale naming; existing skill-directory semantics belong to paths.py/skillforge.py and must not be duplicated. A visibility-gating implementation must wire router.route()'s selected list into an actual content-exposure decision reachable from at least one real harness (the Prime extension and/or hermes_adapter.py), while preserving router.route()'s current advisory consumers (credit.py's P3.13 attribution, model_routing.py's P2.6 quality scoring, cli.py diagnostics) unchanged. Any promotion out of permanent shadow mode must be justified by the existing eval_router acceptance gate (router f1 >= natural f1, no success regression) with fresh, current-session evidence, not by assumption. Preserve P3.15's evidence-provenance hardening (audit:/evaluation:-bound broken-condition evidence) and Lean's candidate/HOLD_SHADOW state; do not begin P3.17.
smallest_genuine_missing_seam: router.route() is a fully proven, deterministic, tested, config-wired sparse top-K shadow router that beats its natural-baseline acceptance gate -- but it has no consumer, in any harness (Python CLI, credit.py, model_routing.py, hermes_adapter.py, or the brainstem Prime extension), that uses its selection to actually restrict which skills' full SKILL.md instructions are exposed to an agent. 'Do not load all skills' and 'descriptor-first, JIT instructions' -- the requirement's own stated deliverable -- are unenforced and unproven live. The smallest complete P3.16 seam is therefore a single real visibility-gate consumer (reachable from at least one live harness) that reads router.route()'s selected list and withholds/defers full-instruction exposure for unselected skills, without altering the router algorithm, its shadow/report-only default for other consumers, or any existing advisory integration.
final_status: P3.16_PARTIAL / router.py's sparse top-K shadow-routing algorithm and its natural-baseline acceptance gate are proven, but no harness anywhere consumes its selection to actually restrict skill visibility ('do not load all skills' is unenforced).
final_independent_validator: P3.16_PARTIAL / smallest genuine missing seam: router-selection-to-SKILL.md-visibility-gate -- no code path anywhere uses router.route()'s output to restrict which skills' full instructions are exposed to an agent in any live harness.
